item.title: IRGC says it shot down US-made drone near Hormuz Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
IRGC says it shot down US-made drone near Hormuz Strait of Hormuz

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that it downed an MQ-1 drone in the airspace east of the Strait of Hormuz, state media reported. 

"The 14th advanced MQ1 drone was intercepted and destroyed by the Revolutionary Guard's new advanced aerospace defense system, under the control of the country's integrated air defense network, in the sky east of the Strait of Hormuz (opposite Sirik)," the announcement carried by IRNA read.

item.title: Obama slams Trump's handling of war on Iran and its toll on the US
item.description:
Obama slams Trump's handling of war on Iran and its toll on the US

Former US president Barack Obama has criticised Donald Trump for his policy in the war on Iran and the toll its had. 

" I didn’t have to fire any missiles. I engaged in diplomacy," he said. 

Refering to the toll of the war on Washington, Obama said: "Our allies and bases have been attacked. Americans have been killed. Hundreds of Americans have been wounded. We have run down our stock of missiles, making us more vulnerable, and Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz."

The fiormer American president added that this is the "reason why the price of oil is up".

Obama added, “This is the reason why the price of oil is up.”

item.title: ‘Time for peace now,’ says Deputy PM of Iraq's Kurdish region
Analysis: Netanyahu is going nowhere until Israel's Palestinians are taken seriously
item.description:
Analysis: Netanyahu is going nowhere until Israel's Palestinians are taken seriously

The results of Israel’s election tell us that Benjamin Netanyahu lost but was not defeated.

He will feel that what he proposed to the Jewish voters - to continue the wars, to maintain the state of emergency - has been accepted.

Netanyahu told voters that the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel was not his fault, and that blame lay on the military instead.

In his telling, Netanyahu stepped in after the failure of the military leadership and made Israel much safer than it was before 7 October. I think it resonated.

Of course, Netanyahu and his allies lost votes compared to the last election in 2022. His coalition appears to be down between eight to 10 seats and short of a majority needed to form a government.

But he has helped force his opponents in the so-called “change campaign” into a minority themselves.

The main event in this election, and it is a positive one, is not only the success of the Joint List alliance of Palestinian parties, but the gains of Mansour Abbas’ Raam, though to a lesser extent.

Read more: Netanyahu is going nowhere until Israel's Palestinians are taken seriously

item.description:
Trump says US 'didn’t start this war' on Iran

US president Donald Trump has claimed that the "didn’t start this war" on Iran, adding that the conflict "should have been taken care of long before I came here".

In late February, Israel and the US launched their war on Iran, despite the Oman-brokered talks at the time centered around Tehran’s nuclear programme.

US-Israeli attacks were also carried out against Iran last year during ongoing discussions.

item.title: ‘Not acceptable’: UN rights chief slams US sanctions on world body’s rapporteur
item.description: UN human rights chief Volker Turk on Wednesday called sanctions imposed on UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese “not acceptable,” Anadolu reports. “You can agree or disagree with someone, but you should never ever sanction them,” said Turk in response to a question from Anadolu at a news conference in New York. “They were appointed by the Human Rights Council as independent experts, and the sanction is just not acceptable,” he said. item.title: Iranian foreign minister says Tehran in talks with mediators to implement 7-day plan with US
item.description: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that Iran is in contact with mediators to review proposals to implement a seven-day plan with the US, Anadolu reports. item.title: World Food Program chief calls Gaza hunger ‘unacceptable’; vows to protect aid workers
item.description: The UN World Food Program (WFP) chief Luke Lindberg said Wednesday that the hunger situation in the Gaza Strip is “unacceptable” as he pledged to defend his staff against attacks, Anadolu reports. Speaking at a news conference at UN headquarters in New York, Lindberg said that “there is a very serious need” in Gaza, citing funding cuts as a major constraint on the agency’s work.
